lead: Real property a person can own — houses, flats, factory-built and floating homes, land and estates, unusual conversions and burial places — organised by property type, with architectural style and regional house tradition as cross-cutting views; commercial and industrial buildings are out, and garden buildings live in Home Fixtures.

b.w: Weighed first by every buying guide; a filter and map, never a department.

b.v: freehold > share of freehold > leasehold / condominium > co-operative
b.w: Determines what is actually owned; checked before survey in most jurisdictions.

b.v: roof, walls, damp, plumbing, wiring, heating (RICS Home Survey Levels 1–3)
b.w: Survey follows title.

b.v: EPC A (92+) > B > C > D > E > F > G
b.w: Running cost and comfort; stored only as a view, never for one home.
Last in the order.

depts.note: Buyer property types first; architectural style and regional tradition are views over the same houses.

b.w: Listing-portal classification (Rightmove, Zillow).
An attribute and a view (Getty AAT style terms), not a kind.

s.brief: Everyday buyer property types. Split old k1 (house) into its attachment types as separate kinds; move its vernacular model list (Siheyuan, Riad, Trulli…) to the 'Regional house traditions' shelf. Each kind: short definition, 't' for sub-types, Wikipedia/Wikidata or Getty AAT source. No maker models.

Detached suburban/resort house, Mediterranean usage; types holiday villa, urban villa.

s.brief: Luxury house types a Knight Frank / Sotheby's buyer searches by name. Definitions from Wikipedia/Getty AAT; add a handful of famous archetypal examples only where they define the type (no listings).

s.brief: A style VIEW, not a buyer type: each kind is a style family whose archetypes are named styles with Getty AAT or Wikipedia sources, era, defining features and regional variants as 'v'. Order by chronology within family. Keep to the styles house-hunters actually use as search terms.

k.brief: Archetypes: Palladian, Georgian, Regency, Federal, Greek Revival, Neoclassical.
Archetypes: Gothic Revival, Italianate, Second Empire, Queen Anne, Romanesque Revival, Edwardian/Baroque Revival.

Archetypes: Colonial (New England, Dutch, French), Cape Cod, Cape Dutch, Queenslander, Federation (Australia), Villa (New Zealand).

s.brief: Absorb old k1's model list and extend. Each kind is a regional group; its archetypes are named vernacular house forms (Wikipedia/Wikidata/UNESCO sources) with region, period, materials. Write a tradition-register entry for each major form (group label 'Vernacular architecture'). Old k1 models: Wealden hall house, bastle house → British; Longère, Frutighaus, Geestharden, Uthland-Frisian, Upper Lusatian, Kulla, Vainakh tower → Continental; Masía, Cortijo, Finca, Casona, Trulli, Riad → Mediterranean; Charleston single house, chattel house, connected farm, upright and wing → Americas; Siheyuan, Yaodong, Assam-type → Asia.

s.brief: Restraint on SKU lists: cut static caravan models to market-covering makers (Willerby, ABI, Swift, Atlas, Carnaby, Pemberton, Victory) as ranges, not 21 SKUs; park model and tiny-house lists to 5–8 makers with one or two signature ranges each. Add kit/prefab house (Huf Haus, Baufritz, Honka, Lindal, historic Sears kit homes as archetypes) and US manufactured home (single/double-wide, Clayton, Skyline Champion). Sources: maker pages, Wikipedia.

s.brief: Non-navigable dwellings only (navigable narrowboats and barges are vehicles, G1). Add regional archetypes: Amsterdam woonboot/woonark, Seattle/Portland floating home, Sausalito houseboat, Kerala/Srinagar houseboat (Dal Lake). Sources: Wikipedia.

s.brief: The findings' luxury land types. Each kind defined from Wikipedia/Wikidata or a reference body (Scottish Land Commission, USDA, FEI); types for sub-uses; archetypal named examples only where they define the type (e.g. Necker Island for private island, Balmoral-type Highland estate). No listings. Old k16 vineyard folds into Vineyard & wine estate; old k26 airstrip into Airpark home.
